newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-US April housing starts seen up slightly.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-US April housing starts seen up slightly.

text.p: April housing starts were seen rising slightly from March to an annualized level of 1.43 million, economists polled by Reuters said.
However, flooding in the Midwest could dent the consensus estimates. Starts came in at a rate of 1.425 million in March.

"Twenty percent of housing starts in the U.S. are in the Midwest and six states there are under water," noted Steven Wieting, economist at Smith Barney Inc. Given the extreme flooding problems, Wieting said he expects data to show starts dropped 1.8 percent to an annual rate of 1.40 million.
"If we're correct, we see building permits higher than starts in April and March. But we'll probably see a nice rebound in May," he said.
Housing starts historically swing by large margins in April -- close to 6.0 percent, Wieting said.
"Given the weather we may see a number well off the mark of consensus," Wieting said.
David Sloan, economist at I.D.E.A., also expected housing starts would fall to 1.40 million on an annualized basis.
"The weather in April was fairly cold and nonfarm payrolls showed weakness in the construction component," Sloan said.
Sloan said there also could be some slippage in multiple starts, which have been high in recent reports.
David Wyss, research director at DRI/McGraw Hill, expected sales to be flat in April at an annualized rate of 1.42 million.
"There's not that many people in North Dokata," Wyss said of one of the states suffering from flooding. He didn't think Midwest flooding would have much of an impact on national activity.
Still, sales have been performing well, he said.
